General.Description:
The Moonveil did not break all at once. It cracked first — a long, slow fracture that ran across the sky over the course of a century, so gradual that most people alive today have never known a whole moon. The shards hang in the atmosphere still, orbiting one another in a slow gravitational dance, their light fragmenting the night into a dozen competing lunar cycles and driving the great tidal magic that all sorcery in the Five Realms depends upon.

But the shards are falling. Slowly, one by one, they are losing altitude. When the last one strikes the ground, the tidal magic will end — and with it, every enchantment, ward, binding, and working that holds the civilisations of the Five Realms together.

Cartographer's assistant Emery Sable discovers this not from any grand prophecy, but from a set of astronomical calculations scrawled in the margin of a stolen shipping ledger. The calculations are forty years old. The person who made them has been dead for thirty-eight.

Shards of the Moonveil is an intimate, beautifully written dark fantasy about the end of one age and the terrifying uncertainty of what comes next. Rowan Ashby has a gift for world-building that feels lived-in rather than constructed, and for characters who feel the weight of what they must do even as they do it.

Extraordinary.
